chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Records with Goodman and Teddy Wilson, and Quincy Jones's Dinah Washington date
summary: Crawford says he recorded with Benny Goodman and Teddy Wilson, and that Quincy Jones hired him and Milt Hinton for a Dinah Washington album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Just play and think like him. See, I didn't have -- I couldn't think like a lot of guys like Sid Catlett, Jo Jones. Even old Krupa wasn't no slouch, you know. He was a digger. He played good drums. I had the fortune to play -- make a record with Benny Goodman with Teddy Wilson on

the piano and Jimmy Crawford on drums. Now, I don't know who was on bass. Maybe Pemberton or somebody. I don't recall. Or Jack -- bass player that played with Goodman's band, good bass player, and just what Quincy Jones said about he hired Jimmy Crawford and Milt Hinton to make a record date with him, not to play in a band. He didn't have a band then. That was before he went to Hollywood.
It happened to be one of Dinah Washington's LPs that we came and made. He said that was the greatest album that he's ever made. That's what Quincy said.
Oh, yeah, right, this (inaudible), yes. Oh, yeah, I have this in a book in fact.
Oh, yeah, good. And so I was just --
